title: Re-hang a sliding cabinet door: top up into its channel, then foot onto the rail
instruction: Hang the loose white door, still facing the robot, in the cabinet's front track and let go of it, leaving the rear door where it is.
context: Sliding doors on sideboards, TV units and wardrobes come off their track for cleaning, for a move or after one jumps out, and go back the way makers describe: Knape & Vogt's sheet for its sliding-door tracks says "Place top of door in guide and swing bottom of door into track", and furniture makers cut the upper grooves considerably deeper than the lower so that a door can be lifted off the lower track (Fine Woodworking No. 172, 2004). The hard parts, in order. (1) The door is taller than the opening (290 mm against 270 mm clear), so it goes in leaned about 10 degrees, top first under the front groove. (2) It is lifted until its top nears the groove's roof: only there does the foot clear the floor's edge and the rail, by 14 mm. (3) The foot is swung in while the top stays between the groove's walls. (4) It is lowered so the 6 mm rail enters the 14 mm groove in its foot, then let go without knocking the hung rear door.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top (z 0); arm bases at y +305 mm and -305 mm. (1) A low media-style cabinet standing on the table, kept small so that its track is within the arms' reach: 16 mm laminated chipboard, brown, open front at x 360 mm, back panel at x 678 mm (318 mm deep), opening 620 mm wide (y -310 to +310), side panels to y +-326 mm. Floor top at z 40 mm (plinth and floor board). Under the 18 mm top board (underside z 350 mm) sit three aluminium-coloured strips 8 mm wide (x) and 40 mm tall (z 310 to 350 mm), 620 mm long, at x 360 to 368, 406 to 414 and 452 to 460 mm: two grooves 38 mm wide and 40 mm deep, centred on x 387 mm (front track) and x 433 mm (rear track); the clear height under the strips is 270 mm. On the floor two aluminium-coloured rails 6 mm wide and 6 mm high, 620 mm long, centred on x 387 and x 433 mm (tops z 46 mm). (2) Rear door, already hung in the rear track over y -300 to +20 mm: white honeycomb-core laminated panel 22 x 320 x 290 mm (thickness x, width y, height z), 0.29 kg, with a groove 14 mm wide and 8 mm deep along its foot; its foot is on the floor with the rail in the groove, its top 20 mm up in the groove. (3) Front door, identical panel (0.29 kg), standing on the table (z 0) with its centre plane at x 337 mm and y from -140 to +180 mm, its pull facing the robot, not touching anything. A bar pull stands off its front face: a 20 x 20 mm aluminium square tube, 140 mm long (along y), centred on the door's width, its centre 170 mm above the foot and 51 mm in front of the door's centre plane, on two 12 x 12 mm posts 30 mm long, 100 mm apart (30 mm gap between bar and face). It is the outer door of the pair, so nothing slides past its pull. Hung, it spans y -20 to +300 mm in the front track. Raised until its top touches the groove's roof its foot is 60 mm above the table top, 14 mm over the rail tops; lowered, its top edge is 20 mm inside the groove. Nothing else is in the scene. Store-bought stock: 22 mm honeycomb door board, 20 x 20 mm aluminium tube, 8 x 40 mm and 6 x 6 mm timber or aluminium strip. Acceptance checks: grooves 38 +-1 mm wide and 40 mm deep (calliper), rails 6 +-0.5 mm, door 0.29 +-0.02 kg (weigh), foot groove 14 +-0.5 mm.
scoring: End state at the last step, from the poses of both doors and the grippers. Front door readings: its top edge (four corners), its underside (corners of both foot strips), its foot groove's centre line at both ends, and its centre plane (11 mm behind its front face) at mid-height. In the groove: the top edge lies between the front groove's walls (+-2 mm) and 6 mm or more above its mouth (every top corner at z 316 mm or higher, none more than 2 mm above the roof at 350, none beyond the opening's ends). Foot down: every corner of the underside is within 3 mm of the floor (z 37 to 43 mm); a strip resting on the rail top reads 6 mm up and fails. Rail in the groove: at both ends of the door the foot groove's centre line is within 5 mm of the rail's centre line (x 387 mm); the strips stop it at 4 mm, and a foot standing on the floor beside the rail is 14 mm or more off. Pull out: the door's outward normal (its pull side) within 60 degrees of facing the robot. Lean: the angle of the door's up axis from vertical. Centre plane: at mid-height within 7 mm of x 387 mm. Rear door kept: it moved 10 mm or less along y and 5 mm along x and leans under 4 degrees. Hands off: for the last 1 s both grippers' fingers are 30 mm or more from the front door. Still: over the last 1 s neither door moves 5 mm or turns 5 degrees. Zero unless the hands are off and both doors still (and zero for a state that is not finite), and zero if at any moment the rear door was knocked out (its lowest underside corner under z 30 mm, leaning over 10 degrees, moved over 20 mm in x or 60 mm in y). Otherwise: 1.0 for in the groove, foot down, rail in the groove, pull out, centre plane within 7 mm, lean under 3 degrees, inside the opening, rear door kept; 0.5 for in the groove, foot down and pull out with lean under 8 degrees but not 1.0 (lean 3 to 8 degrees, the foot beside the rail, the centre plane over 7 mm off, or an end outside the opening); 0.25 for in the groove otherwise (foot up on the rail top, leaning out, or the door turned round with its pull inside), and for any higher tier with the rear door moved; 0 otherwise (door on the table, in the rear groove, on top of the cabinet). Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0. Real trial: top depth with a depth gauge or a pencil line on the door's edge, foot height with a 3 mm feeler gauge along the underside, rail in the groove with a rule at both ends of the door from the rail's front face to the door's front face at the floor (3 to 13 mm), centre plane with a rule from the track's front edge (x 360 mm) to the door's front face at mid-height (16 +-7 mm), lean with a 3 degree and an 8 degree angle gauge, rear door with a rule and a 4 degree gauge, a 30 mm spacer against each hand, and a 1 s video for stillness.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, friction 0.4 on every surface (est). The track is shop-built the way furniture makers build one (top grooves deeper than the door needs, so it lifts off the lower track), not a bought kit; it has 8 mm of play each side of the door at the top and 4 mm each side of the 6 mm rail in the 14 mm foot groove (est). Plain 22 mm panels (honeycomb as a solid box, 0.29 kg, est), no rollers, stops or soft-close. Rails and foot groove are exact boxes; the cabinet is solid.
reset_notes: Hang the rear door (foot groove over the rear rail, top in the rear groove, y -300 to +20 mm). Stand the front door on the table at the start spot, pull facing the robot, centre plane at x 337 mm, y -140 to +180 mm, with a rule. Check the grooves and rails are clean and the pull is tight. Nothing is consumed; honeycomb doors dent at their foot, so swap a dented one.
